So that a database never mixes things up, every row gets a unique number: the ID. And instead of copying names again and again, you simply point to this number – that is how tables are connected.
Eine Nummer, die jede Zeile einer Tabell: A number that each row of a table has, exactly once.
Kommt nur ein einziges Mal vor. Es gibt: Appears only once. Nothing can be mixed up.
Die Spalte, die jede Zeile eindeutig mac: The column that makes every row unique – usually id.
Eine Spalte, die auf die ID in einer and: A column that points to the ID in another table, e.g. leser_id.
Auf etwas zeigen: leser_id = 7 verweist: To point to something: leser_id = 7 refers to the reader with ID 7.
How two tables are connected, e.g. “one reader borrows many books”.
